## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
In broader doctrinal developments of early Theravāda Abhidharma, scholars note that the *Peṭakopadesa* (provisionally assigned to the first century BCE) articulates a causal theory in which cause (*hetu*) is understood as internal "own-nature" (*svabhāva*) and condition (*paccaya*) as external "other-nature" (*parabhāva*) [Sprung 1973].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral connect the chapter directly to sections of the counterpart hermeneutical work, the *Nettippakaraṇa*—including the *Saṅgahavāra* (Ne 1), *Uddesavāra* (Ne 2), *Yuttihāravibhaṅga* (Ne 6), and *Vevacanahāravibhaṅga* (Ne 13)—as well as to the *Suttavebhaṅgiya* (Pe 9) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus strongly confirms these affiliations through extensive Pali-internal text reuse, showing substantial shared passages with Ne 2 (longest match §10.4–22.1_0 ↔ §0.2–10.3_1), the *Hārasampātabhūmi* (Pe 8), and Pe 9, along with massive shared material across canonical Abhidhamma and Nikāya collections such as the *Nidāna Saṁyutta* (SN 12), the *Paṭiccasamuppādavibhaṅga* (Vb 6), the *Saccavibhaṅga* (Vb 4), and the *Sacca Saṁyutta* (SN 56), and later commentaries including the *Nettivibhāvinī* and the *Nettippakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language machine alignments in DharmaNexus additionally align the text with Sanskrit and Tibetan treatises—including the *Saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtaviniścaya* (D3897), the *Lalitavistara*, and the *Udānavarga*—as well as Chinese Āgama sutras in the *Madhyama Āgama* (T 26), *Ekottarika Āgama* (T 125), and *Saṃyukta Āgama* (T 99) [DharmaNexus].
